strategy.thesis: The venture capital fund of Tel Aviv University, the first university-affiliated VC in Israel; invests pre-seed/seed in startups founded mainly by TAU students, faculty and alumni, modeled on US university funds (MIT, Stanford, UC Berkeley).

summary.en: TAU Ventures is Tel Aviv University's venture capital fund, the first university-affiliated VC in Israel. Launched in 2018 with a $20M first fund and a $50M (up to $70M) second fund in 2021, it makes pre-seed/seed investments of up to $1M, primarily in startups by TAU students, alumni and faculty.

summary.en: Fresh Fund (fresh.fund) is Israel's first university-focused venture fund, founded in 2016 by Zaki Djemal as a student-analyst network with chapters at Hebrew University, TAU, IDC Herzliya, Technion and Lev Academic College. It has since become one of Israel's largest dedicated pre-seed funds, writing first checks of roughly $300K to ambitious (often first-time) Israeli founders.

Managed by Hebrew University Business School students and affiliated with the Asper Center, it invests in early-stage impact startups operating in Jerusalem and/or founded by HUJI alumni, across FoodTech, AgTech, MedTech, BioTech, Industry 4.0 and EdTech.

strategy.thesis: Technion's hub for biomedical innovation: accelerates the development and commercialization of biomedical technologies, medical devices and life-sciences inventions conceived by Technion researchers, students, faculty and alumni, and spins them out as companies.

summary.en: AMIT (Alfred Mann Institute at the Technion) is the Technion's biomedical innovation hub, established in 2006 with a landmark $100M endowment from American billionaire Dr. Alfred Mann. It accelerates the development and commercialization of biomedical, medical-device and life-science inventions by Technion researchers, students and alumni, spinning out companies such as Accellta.

summary.en: Technion Seed is a seed-stage incubator/investment vehicle jointly owned by four venture capital funds (Battery Ventures, Vertex, SCP-Vitalife, ProSeed) together with the Technion R&D Foundation. It made initial investments of up to roughly $1M in early-stage Technion-linked ventures across deep tech, medical devices, energy and materials. The vehicle is now permanently closed; its last investment was in 2022 and last exit (ENvizion Medical) in 2025.

strategy.thesis: The Technion's non-profit research, development and commercialization foundation; parent of the T3 tech-transfer arm and a backer of Technion-linked investment vehicles, supporting spinouts and startups built on Technion IP from early stages through Round B.

summary.en: The Technion Research & Development Foundation (TRDF) is the non-profit foundation of the Technion that manages its research, development and commercialization activity. It is the parent of the T3 technology-transfer arm and a co-owner/backer of Technion investment vehicles (e.g. Technion Seed), supporting spinouts and startups built on Technion IP. In 2017 TRDF and UG Capital Management announced a $200M venture fund (later reported cancelled).

summary.en: embARC Ventures is the healthtech accelerator/fund of Sheba Medical Center's ARC Innovation Center, launched September 2024 and backed by Ilex Medical. It guarantees a $250K investment per startup (for the first time in Israel on predetermined terms: 7% equity for the initial $125K, the remaining $125K convertible) to cohorts of 5-10 early-stage Israeli and global healthtech startups over a ~3-month program, with clinical access at Sheba and a US roadshow. Managed by Dan Shwarzman.

summary.en: Kidum is the technology-transfer and commercialization unit of the Agricultural Research Organization (Volcani Institute), Israel's largest agricultural research institute and an affiliate of the Ministry of Agriculture.
